questions.question: What does `@supports (display: grid) { ... }` actually check?
options: The user agent string to guess the browser name
Whether the current browser itself understands that property/value pair, applying the block only if it does
Whether the user's screen is wide enough for a grid layout
Whether a polyfill script has loaded
questions.explanation: @supports performs real feature detection against the browser's own capabilities, which is more reliable than inferring support from a spoofable user agent string.

questions.question: In progressive enhancement, what is the baseline experience built from?
options: The newest, most feature-rich version of the UI
Something that works everywhere, typically semantic HTML and basic CSS, with enhancements layered on top for capable browsers
A browser-specific version for each major browser
questions.explanation: Progressive enhancement starts from a guaranteed-to-work baseline and adds capability for browsers that support more, rather than hoping a rich experience degrades safely.

questions.question: How does graceful degradation differ in direction from progressive enhancement?
options: They are exactly the same technique with a different name
Graceful degradation starts from the full, modern experience and adds fallbacks for when something isn't supported, the reverse direction of progressive enhancement
Graceful degradation only applies to JavaScript, never CSS
Graceful degradation means ignoring older browsers entirely
questions.explanation: Progressive enhancement builds up from a baseline; graceful degradation builds down from the ideal experience, providing a fallback path for unsupported cases.

questions.question: Why check a feature on caniuse.com against your project's browserslist before relying on it?
options: It's purely a formality with no practical value
To concretely know whether your actual supported-browser audience needs a fallback, rather than guessing or over-engineering for browsers nobody uses
caniuse.com is required for @supports to function
It replaces the need for any testing
questions.explanation: Real support data lets you make an informed, audience-specific decision instead of either skipping a useful feature unnecessarily or shipping something that silently breaks for real users.
